newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan extends $33 million in debt relief to Burma.
newsitem.headline: Japan extends $33 million in debt relief to Burma.

text.p: Japan has agreed to provide Burma with four billion yen ($33.0 million) in a debt-relief grant under an ongoing 10-year-old programme to help ease the country's debt burden arising from repayment of yen loans, the Foreign Ministry said on Monday.
The grant covers the April-September period of last year, and matches the amount Rangoon spent liquidating earlier debts, the ministry said.

Since Burma was declared a least less-developed country (LLDC) in 1987, Japan has extended debt-relief grants to cover interest payments and repayments of part of the principal of its yen loans to Rangoon.
Japan extended the last similar grant of four billion yen last November. ($1=121 yen)
